tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-27 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Neutral at industry level because it is split, carried. Banks: the UK Financial Policy Committee ruling is favourable for cost of equity and Jefferies (D. Farr, 26-Nov) sees 'the mother of all comebacks' into 2027, against consensus cuts and HSBC, ING and Societe Generale selling AI loans (MacroStrategy, 26-Nov); insurance was not spoken to. Relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior). Banks C and Insurance B carry the view; Alternative finance D. No change.

sector.why: Neutral, carried, with Richard's question re-asked and both legs read: the margin leg leads (the UK Financial Policy Committee ruling favourable for cost of equity and Jefferies' D. Farr, 26-Nov, expecting 'the mother of all comebacks' into 2027) while the credit leg is AI-concentrated and being sold down by the banks themselves (HSBC, ING and Societe Generale listing AI loans for sale; MacroStrategy, 26-Nov), with consensus cuts having hit valuations and no default wave read. Relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; A prior), the market has cooled. 25 of 173 Pool stocks are banks. Counter-case unchanged on both sides; back to B on French spreads under 100 basis points or a second house joining the comeback call; to D on a default wave or a general European spread widening.

geography.why: Overweight, carried: the 15% inclusive US tariff on Switzerland is 'largely as expected' (Goldman, 25-Nov), Roche is Kepler's pharma top pick and 'the clear AI leader in pharma' (26-Nov), and the Swiss market's low-beta character is the rotation this row was set on; the Swiss National Bank and the franc were not read. Counter-case: the franc takes 2 to 3 points a year off a Swiss exporter's reported profit. Back to C if the SNB joins the hikers or the franc reverses.
